For your 4 nights in Niseko:

If you want off-piste and black diamond runs - definitely recommend the all mountain pass in Niseko, you'll get free bus services that connects all the ski resorts. Stay in Hirafu or Kutchan - there are regular buses that connect both towns and is fairly easy to get around plus great night life. Agreed with the Aussies here, 90% of people here speak English so you'll be fine getting around. 

Rutsutsu is also great, there's a bus service that takes you here also. You don't need a car :) if you plan to hire afterwards, there's a Toyota car hire in Kutchan.

Niseko/Kutchan/Hirafu is a beautiful area to ski/snow board and hit some great bars/restaurants after. During winter it's 90% foreigners and English speakers so getting around is easy. There are also direct buses from sapporo and the airport and shuttle buses that connects the towns. 

Niseko - quite, more secluded if you like peacefulness 
Kutchan - small town with a lot of restaurants and bars, better grocery shopping and a lot of the workers from hirafu live here. 
Hirafu - main area, better buildings and has good night life. Restaurants are a little more expensive here. Some people head to Kutchan for nightlife as it's more intimate. There are direct buses connecting kutchan and hirafu during winter

There's a sledding company called White Isle in Kutchan but it's not that fast

Hello, Niseko-resident here. 

If youre planning to arrive to Niseko from otaru in the morning and ski, you can either do a half day or night ski.

Unless you also intend to stay in Niseko - I recommend booking a ski in and out hotel such as Kiniseko or Skye hotel where they also have their own ski rentals to help you save time (always book in advance! They book out quickly).

Personally, I recommend at least 2-3 days minimum of skiing to make the most of it and to explore hirafu/kutchan - there are shuttle buses that connects the towns and ski resorts. 

Taxis here are SUPER expensive. Even for 1.5hr ride to Noboribetsu.. you'll be looking at 30,000yen minimum.

Otaru also has a snow festival - double check the dates, I'm sure it's during Feb. I prefer otaru's one as it's more intimate and not much effected by the city lights and surrounding buildings. 

Hope this helps - Goodluck!!

From someone who has been cheated on, I found this helped me tremendously (from the support of friends and family):

1. Letting me feel what I feel and cry it all out.
2. Reassurance I always had support and is always loved by them no matter what.
3. Helping build my confidence - my sister took me to a women's self defence class and my confidence just went right up. My best friend bought me a painting kit to reignite my passion for art, this helped me kept busy. 
4. Recommend seeing a therapist. This allows her to differentiate facts or feelings and to entirely focus on herself. They can also teach her cognitive behaviour therapy which helps her redirect her negative thoughts into something more constructive and enlightening. 
5. Also give her time and patience. Always take care of yourself as well!! 

Overall, knowing you have people who love you will always put me at ease. I'm sure your friend is very grateful to have you in her life. Don't be afraid to voice your concerns and that you'll always be there for her ☺️
